messages:
lucy: Running into a weird failure when using the async Python SDK against Dedicated behind our corp HTTP proxy. Synchronous client workaround (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) exists, but our async tests blow up. Anybody familiar with aiohttp/ssl_context quirks?

omar: Can you paste the error + how you're instantiating the async client? Async transports often need explicit SSLContext wiring.

lucy: Error and snippet below. We pass `verify` like the sync client.

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/e2e_async.py", line 18, in <module>
    asyncio.run(main())
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/asyncio/runners.py", line 44, in run
    return loop.run_until_complete(main)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/asyncio/base_events.py", line 642, in run_until_complete
    return future.result()
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1123)
```

Client init (async):
```py
from redwood.async_client import AsyncRedwoodClient
client = AsyncRedwoodClient(
    api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'),
    base_url='https://dedicated.internal',
    verify='/etc/ssl/certs/company_chain.pem',
    proxies={'https': 'http://proxy.corp:3128'}
)
await client.health.check()
```

natalie: Which aiohttp / urllib3 version? Also, are tests running in CI with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set? Async clients using aiohttp won't read REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, so the env trick only helps sync code.

lucy: aiohttp 3.8.4, python 3.10. In CI we didn't set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for async runners. Local quick manual set helps for sync but not for async.

omar: Confirmed pattern: aiohttp requires an SSLContext passed to the TCPConnector, or it uses the default system context which won't pick up a custom cafile unless SSL_CERT_FILE or SSL_CERT_DIR env vars are set. Workarounds: (A) build SSLContext and pass into client connector, (B) set SSL_CERT_FILE=... in env before process start.

natalie: Example of (A):
```py
import ssl
from aiohttp import TCPConnector, ClientSession
from redwood.async_client import AsyncRedwoodClient

ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/certs/company_chain.pem')
conn = TCPConnector(ssl=ctx)
# If our SDK supports a session/connector param we can inject it
async with AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key=..., base_url=..., connector=conn) as client:
    await client.health.check()
```
If the SDK doesn't expose connector/ssl_context, you get the verify failure.

lucy: Tried constructing an AsyncRedwoodClient that way by monkeypatching internal session, worked. So the root cause is SDK doesn't expose async ssl_context/connector parity with sync client.

omar: Sounds like a feature parity + bug. Two things: (1) doc the env var caveat for async vs sync and add an async snippet that shows creating TCPConnector with ssl context, (2) add a public `ssl_context` / `connector` parameter to AsyncRedwoodClient constructor so callers don't need hacks. Also suggest `ca_bundle` string param that accepts a cafile path for convenience.

natalie: I'll file the issue and include a minimal repro and CI notes. Also note: when proxies perform TLS interception the cert presented by the proxy must be in the chain we trust. Recommend callout in onboarding checklist to validate chain order (root last) and to test with curl + openssl s_client to inspect the cert presented.

natalie: Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/1999 "async: expose ssl_context/connector and ca_bundle for aiohttp-based client (proxy+custom CA support)" with repro steps and sample snippet.

devops-bot: CI note: set SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/company_chain.pem in async job matrix as short-term mitigation. Created CI change request MR: #1247.

lucy: Great. I'll add the async snippet to the devex quickstarts and include the TCPConnector example + note about env var differences between requests and aiohttp. Also will add a small test case to our e2e suite that runs with SSL_CERT_FILE set to validate the onboarding checklist.

omar: One more subtlety: some users provide a concatenated bundle with leaf first; OpenSSL / aiohttp may treat that differently than curl. Recommend we validate bundle ordering in our docs and offer a tiny script to normalize a bundle (concatenate intermediates then root last).

lucy: Will include that script in the PR. Thanks all!
